newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Vasakronan bids for Gotic in Swedish property deal.
newsitem.headline: Vasakronan bids for Gotic in Swedish property deal.

text.p: Swedish state-owned real estate group Vasakronan on Friday placed a cash bid worth 773 million crowns ($96.4 million) on rival Gotic in another reshuffle in the Swedish property market.

Vasakronan bid 19.75 crowns per Gotic A share and 19 crowns per B share, corresponding to a premium of 12.9 percent and 12.4 percent to the last price paid for the shares on August 1 and 5, respectively, the company said in a statement.
Gotic shares were suspended on the Stockholm Stock Exchange on Wednesday and resumed trading at 0910 GMT on Friday. The bid lifted the shares 1.80 crowns higher to 18.70 by 1100 GMT.
Gotic owners holding 39.5 percent of the equity and 57.1 percent of the votes in the company have given the bid a nod and Gotic's board recommends shareholders accept it.
Vasakronan's move is in line with the group's focus on office buildings in the 15 towns in Sweden.
"We estimate there is a significant development potential in Gotic's real estate holdings," Vasakronan president Hakan Bryngelson said in the statement.
"Through the acquisition Vasakronan will become the leading office property owner in Malmo (on the southern tip of Sweden)."
Vasakronan sold 194 properties outside the 15 targeted towns in June.
After the buy, Vasakronan's rental income in the 15 towns will amount to about two billion crowns while its equity-to-assets ratio will fall to 37 percent from 41.5.
Vasakronan's move follows a Wednesday bid by real estate group Diligentia on Hufvudstaden International.
Diligentia offered one of its shares for 13 in the target company, a 25 percent premium on the average share price of Hufvudstaden International in the past 10 days.
Owners representing 77 percent of Hufvudstaden International backed the bid.
Dilgentia said it planned to split up the new group into an international group and a Swedish company and list them separately.

The book value of the two groups' international divisions at the end of 1996 totalled 11.6 billion crowns, of which Brussels, Paris and London accounted for 71 percent, while the book value of Swedish properties totalled 10.4 billion.
-- Birgitta Forsberg, Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700 1006 ($ = 8.019 Swedish Crowns)
